sanskrit: ekapadī dvipadī sā catuṣpady aṣṭāpadī navapadī babhūvuṣī | sahasrākṣarā bhuvanasya paṅktis tyasyāḥ samudrā adhi vi kṣaranti ||
english: She who has become one-footed, two-footed, four-footed, eight-footed, nine-footed — the verse of the universe with a thousand syllables: from her the oceans flow forth in all directions.

sanskrit: ārohan dyām amṛtaḥ prāva me vaca ut tvā yajñā brahmapūtā vahanti | ghṛtaṃ pibantaṃ harayas tvā vahanti ||
english: Ascending to the sky, the immortal one protected my speech. The brahman-purified sacrifices carry you upward. The bay steeds carry you as you drink ghee.

sanskrit: veda tat te amartti yat ta ākramaṇaṃ divi | yat te sadhasthaṃ parame vyoman ||
english: I know that undying thing of yours — your foothold in the sky, your dwelling-place in the highest heaven.

sanskrit: sūryo dyāṃ sūryaḥ pṛthivīṃ sūrya āpo 'ti paśyati | sūryo bhūtasyaikaṃ cakṣur ā ruroha divaṃ mahīm ||
english: The sun looks out over the sky; the sun looks over the earth; the sun looks over the waters. The sun, the one eye of all beings, has ascended the great sky.

sanskrit: urvīr āsan paridhayo vedir bhūmir akalpata | tatraitāv agnī ādhatta himaṃ ghraṃsaṃ ca rohitaḥ ||
english: The enclosures were vast; the earth became the vedi. There Rohita set down these two fires — the cold dew and the blazing heat.

sanskrit: himaṃ ghraṃsaṃ cādhāya yūpān kṛtvā parvatān | varṣājyāv agnī ījāte rohitasya svarvidaḥ ||
english: Having set down the cold and the blaze and made the mountains into sacrificial posts, the two fires — knowers of the heavenly world — sacrifice with rain as ghee for Rohita.

sanskrit: svarvido rohitasya brahmaṇāgniḥ samāhitaḥ | tasmād ghraṃsas tasmād dhimas tasmād yajño ajāyata ||
english: For Rohita the sky-knower, Agni was established through brahman. From him arose the blaze, from him the cold, from him the sacrifice was born.

sanskrit: brahmaṇāgniḥ saṃidhāno brahmavṛddho brahmahutaḥ | brahmeddhāv agnī ījāte rohitasya svarvidaḥ ||
english: Agni kindled by brahman, grown great by brahman, fed with oblations of brahman — the two fires kindled by brahman sacrifice for Rohita, knower of the sky.

sanskrit: apsv anyaḥ samāhitaḥ satye anyaḥ samāhitaḥ | (…) ||
english: One is established in the waters; another is established in truth. [The rest of the verse is lacunose in the manuscript.]

sanskrit: yaṃ vātaḥ pariśumbhati yam indro brahmaṇaspatiḥ | brahmeddhāv agnī ījāte rohitasya svarvidaḥ ||
english: Him whom the wind adorns, him whom Indra and Brahmaṇaspati adorn — the two fires kindled by brahman sacrifice for Rohita, knower of the sky.

sanskrit: vediṃ bhūmiṃ kalpayitvā divaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇām | ghraṃsaṃ tad agniṃ kṛtvā cakāra viśvam ātmanvad varṣeṇājyena rohitaḥ ||
english: Having fashioned the earth as the vedi and the sky as the south, having made that blaze the fire, Rohita made everything animated, with rain as the ghee.

sanskrit: varṣam ājyaṃ ghraṃso agnir vedir bhūmir akalpata | tatraitān parvatām̐ agnir gīrbhir ūrdhvām̐ akalpayat ||
english: Rain became the ghee, the blaze became the fire, the earth became the vedi. There Agni fashioned these mountains upright with his hymns.

sanskrit: gīrbhir ūrdhvān kalpayitvā rohito bhūmim abravīt | tvad idaṃ sarvaṃ jāyatāṃ yad bhūtaṃ yac ca bhāvyam ||
english: Having fashioned them upright with hymns, Rohita addressed the earth: "From you let all this be born — whatever has existed and whatever shall be."

sanskrit: sa yajñaḥ prathamo bhūto bhavyo ajāyata | tasmād dha yajña idaṃ sarvaṃ yat kiṃ cedaṃ virocate rohitena rṣiṇābhṛtam ||
english: That sacrifice was the first being, the first to be born as what will be. From that sacrifice everything shines forth here — whatever Rohita the seer has upheld.

sanskrit: ud asya ketavo divi śukrā bhrājanta īrate | ādityasya nṛcakṣaso mahivratasya mīduṣaḥ ||
english: His bright banners rise and blaze in the sky — those of Āditya who sees men, who holds the great vow, who is bountiful.

sanskrit: diśāṃ prajñānaṃ svarayantam arciṣā supakṣam āśuṃ patayantam arṇave | stavāma sūryaṃ bhuvanasya gopāṃ yo raśmibhir diśa ābhāti sarvāḥ ||
english: The knower of the directions, resounding with his flame, well-winged, flying swiftly across the sea — we praise the sun, guardian of the world, who illumines all the directions with his rays.

sanskrit: yat prāṅ pratyaṅ svadhayā yāsi śībhaṃ nānārūpe ahanī karṣi māyayā | tad āditya mahi tat te mahi śravo yad eko viśvaṃ pari bhūma jāyase ||
english: That you go swiftly eastward and westward by your own power, and draw the two days of varied form by your māyā — that, O Āditya, is your greatness; great is your renown, that you alone are born encompassing the entire world.

sanskrit: vipaścitaṃ taraṇiṃ bhrājamānaṃ vahanti yaṃ haritaḥ sapta bahvīḥ | stutād yam atrir divam unnināya taṃ tvā paśyema pariyantam ājim ||
english: Him the wise, the swift, the blazing — whom the seven great bay mares carry — whom Atri, upon being praised, raised to the sky — may we see you, him, traversing your course.

sanskrit: mā tvā dabhan pariyantam ājiṃ sugena durgam ati yāhi śībham | divaṃ ca sūrya pṛthivīṃ ca devīm ahorātre vimimāno yad eṣi ||
english: Let no one deceive you as you traverse your course; pass swiftly through ease and through hardship. As you go, O sun, measuring out both the sky and the divine earth with day and night —

sanskrit: svasti te sūrya carase rathāya yenobhāv antau pariyāsi sadyaḥ | yaṃ te vahanti harito vahiṣṭhās tam ā roha sukham āśvaśvam ||
english: Good fortune to your moving chariot, O sun, with which you circuit both ends at once; mount that chariot comfortably, drawn by the best of your bay horses, swift as thought.

sanskrit: sukhaṃ sūrya ratham aṃśumantaṃ syonaṃ suvahnim adhi tiṣṭha vājinam | yaṃ te vahanti harito vahiṣṭhāḥ śatam aśvā yadi vā sapta bahvīḥ ||
english: O sun, mount comfortably the radiant chariot, pleasant, well-harnessed, of prize horses — the one your finest bay mares draw: a hundred steeds, or indeed the seven great ones.

sanskrit: sapta sūryo harito yātave rathe hiraṇyatvacaso bṛhatīr ayukta | amoci śukro rajasaḥ parastād vidhūya devas tamo divam āruhat ||
english: The sun yoked seven great golden-skinned bay mares to the chariot for the journey. The bright one, shaking off darkness, freed himself beyond the realm of dust, and the god ascended to the sky.

sanskrit: ut ketunā bṛhatā devā āgann apāvṛk tamo 'bhi jyotir aśrait | divyaḥ suparṇa sthavīro vy akhyad adityāḥ putro bhuvanāni viśvā ||
english: The gods came with a great banner; removing darkness they advanced toward the light. The heavenly great-winged one, the mighty, surveyed all the worlds — the son of Aditi.

sanskrit: udyan raśmīn ā tanuṣe prajāḥ sarvā vi paśyati | ubhā samudrau kratunā vi bhāsi sarvāṃ lokān paribhūr bhrājamānaḥ ||
english: Rising, you stretch out your rays; you behold all living beings. With your power you illuminate both oceans, blazing you encompass all the worlds.

sanskrit: pūrvāparaṃ carato māyayaitau śiśū kundānā pari yāto arṇavam | viśvāny anyo bhuvanābhi vaste hairaṇyair anyaṃ harito vahanti ||
english: These two young ones, yearning, travel around the sea by māyā, moving east and west. One wraps itself around all the worlds; the bay mares carry the other with their golden trappings.

sanskrit: divi tvātrir dhārayat sūryā māsāya kartave | sa eṣi sudhṛtas tapan svar bhūtāvacākaśat ||
english: Atri held you in the sky, O sun, to make the months. Thus you go, well-sustained, blazing with heat upon the heavenly light, shining upon all beings.

sanskrit: ubhāv antau sam arṣati vatsaḥ saṃmātarāv iva | nanv etad itaḥ purā brahma devā amī viduḥ ||
english: The calf flows together toward both ends, as toward two mothers. Surely even now the gods yonder have known this brahman since of old.

sanskrit: yat samudram anu śritaṃ tat siṣāsati sūryaḥ | adhvāsya vitato mahān pūrvaś cāparaś ca yaḥ ||
english: What is leaning toward the sea — that the sun desires to win. His path is stretched out vast, the one that goes both east and west.

sanskrit: taṃ sam āpnoti jūtibhis tasmān nāpa cikitsati | tenāmṛtasya bhakṣaṃ devānāṃ nāva rundhate ||
english: He reaches it with his swift movements; therefore he does not fall short. Thereby he does not obstruct the gods' share of immortality.

sanskrit: ud u tyaṃ jātavedasaṃ devaṃ vahanti ketavaḥ | dṛśe viśvāya sūryam ||
english: And behold — the rays carry yonder god Jātavedas, the sun, for all the world to see.
